name: italian tomato sauce
instructions:
THE ITALIAN TOMATO SAUCE MEGA RECIPE — five variants, merged 2026-11-13 from bolognese + weeknight vegetarian ragu + marcella gnocchi sauce + spaghetti and meatballs + pasta piperade:
- VARIANT A — BOLOGNESE: Marcella Hazan's meat ragu (pass).
- VARIANT B — WEEKNIGHT VEGETARIAN RAGU: the no-ceremony crumbles ragu (pass).
- VARIANT C — MARCELLA GNOCCHI SAUCE: the 3-ingredient butter-onion-tomato sauce (pass).
- VARIANT D — SPAGHETTI AND MEATBALLS: unattempted.
- VARIANT E — PASTA PIPERADE: the blended pepper-tomato sauce, spanish lean (pass).

THE TOMATO FORMS SPLIT HARD BY BUILD — see the build-dependent rulings note before substituting anything.

=== VARIANT A — BOLOGNESE (MARCELLA HAZAN'S RAGU — PASS) ===

TWO BOLOGNESE VARIANTS. Both share: tomato base + a protein + wine + soffrito-style aromatics + long simmer intent + pasta. Variant A is the canonical bolognese (Marcella); VARIANT B IS MY BOLOGNESE — the core recipe of this file, rebuilt around the meat-thing-minimum rule (see below). (Nisha's and ATK's vegetarian recipes are kept as CONTEXT in the notes.)

LENTILS, MUSHROOMS, AND WALNUTS ARE SECONDARY/OK in this recipe (see notes — the allowance does NOT extend to [[french-beef-and-mushroom-stew]]). The protein slot is a meat thing, real or fake — but IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND BEEF IS BANNED (clashing — it ages horribly; see notes). ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is the best fake.

=== VARIANT A — MARCELLA BOLOGNESE (CANONICAL) ===

The load-bearing recipe in this family. Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking. If 'bolognese' means one thing in this cookbook, it's this one.

INGREDIENTS:
- vegetable oil + butter (the fat)
- yellow onions, celery, carrots — finely diced soffrito
- ground beef (or abbots ground beef as the substitute)
- milk
- nutmeg
- WHITE wine (Marcella's canonical; red wine also appears in some bolognese traditions — see WINE note)
- canned tomatoes
- black pepper
- pasta (traditionally tagliatelle, not spaghetti)
- parmesan cheese for serving

TECHNIQUE — MARCELLA'S NON-NEGOTIABLES:
1. Cook the beef ONLY until it loses raw color. Do NOT brown it. Browning gives a different (and lesser) ragu.
2. Milk goes in BEFORE wine. The milk coats the meat and protects it from the wine acid; reversing the order changes the texture.
3. Bare-simmer for THREE+ HOURS uncovered. Splash in water if it dries out. The long uncovered simmer is what makes it a bolognese; cutting time turns it into a generic meat sauce.
4. Fat should separate at the end. That's the visual signal you're done.

=== VARIANT B — MY BOLOGNESE (THE CORE RECIPE) ===

Mine. The current build:

- SOFFRITO: celery / onion, in OLIVE OIL + BUTTER. NO CARROTS — too sweet (see notes).
- GARLIC.
- PROTEIN — THE MEAT-THING-MINIMUM RULE: some kind of VEGAN BEEF is the BARE MINIMUM — ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is best. It's like a french beef stew — you need a meat thing even if it's fake. (Real ground beef obviously qualifies.) IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND BEEF IS BANNED — gummy, candy-like, artificial the day after (see notes).
- MILK + NUTMEG (watch the nutmeg — it can embitter; see the bitterness note).
- WINE DEGLAZE.
- SAUCE: CANNED TOMATO SAUCE — not tomato paste, not crushed tomatoes (this is where I think Nisha is wrong). HALF A CAN is generally enough, with ENOUGH MILK THAT IT'S CREAMY.
- HERBS: THYME + OREGANO are primary. ROSEMARY goes well here when there's ACTUAL MEAT in it.
- TOASTED WALNUTS: secondary option — toast first, don't overdo it (walnuts can embitter).
- IF VEGETARIAN: the recipe benefits from PORCINI POWDER + NUTRITIONAL YEAST — and A LOT of porcini powder makes a difference (pub-lentils rules).
- DARK BALSAMIC VINEGAR — Nisha's discovery; the dish is incomplete without it. STAYS.
- CHEESE at the end: GRUYERE (funky — preferred) or parmesan.
- Serve with a PASTA WATER EMULSION.

=== VARIANT B — WEEKNIGHT VEGETARIAN RAGU (PASS) ===

The weeknight base-substrate system: cook a big batch of protein pasta once, keep it all week, and finish portions in different directions.

=== THE BASE SUBSTRATE ===

1. Cook AS MUCH PASTA AS POSSIBLE.
2. SAUTÉ an entire pack of VEGAN BEEF CRUMBLES (or ground beef) in OLIVE OIL with GARLIC and simple herbs — THYME/OREGANO.
3. TOSS the pasta with the meat and PASTA WATER.
4. SAVE IN A TUB — this is the substrate for the whole week.

=== VARIANT A — TOMATO ===

Tomato with MUSHROOMS, ONIONS, or EGGPLANT: sauté them, then add to the substrate.

=== VARIANT B — CREAM (VEGAN) + GREENS ===

CASHEW CREAM, with SPINACH or CHARD. (The vegan silken tofu sauce option is KILLED — see notes.)

=== VARIANT C — GREEN + LEMON ===

Add STEAMED BROCCOLI or GREEN BEANS and LEMON.

=== VARIANT C — MARCELLA GNOCCHI SAUCE (THE 3-INGREDIENT SAUCE — PASS) ===

Marcella Hazan's famous three-ingredient tomato sauce, kept in the cookbook as THE GNOCCHI SAUCE — she recommends the basic tomato/onion/butter sauce be used on GNOCCHI in particular, and it's very simple, requiring no blender. From Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking.

(The rest of the tomato pasta sauce family — sicilian pesto rosso, vodka sauce, pasta piperade, marcella eggplant sauce — is RETIRED to retired/; see notes.)

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 28-oz can whole peeled tomatoes (San Marzano ideal — canned whole, not diced, not paste)
- 1 medium yellow onion, peeled and halved (NOT chopped — kept in halves)
- 5 tablespoons unsalted butter
- salt to taste
- gnocchi (Marcella's recommended pairing — the reason this recipe survives; short pasta shapes also fine)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Combine tomatoes, butter, onion halves, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan.
2. Simmer uncovered on low for ~45 minutes, stirring occasionally and crushing the tomatoes with the back of a spoon as they soften.
3. Fish out and discard the onion halves before serving (they've done their aromatic job).
4. Toss with cooked gnocchi (or short pasta).

=== VARIANT D — SPAGHETTI AND MEATBALLS (UNATTEMPTED) ===

Real meatballs in a crushed-tomato sauce over spaghetti. The meatballs are a classic panade build; the sauce base is CRUSHED TOMATOES or CRUSHED FIRE-ROASTED TOMATOES, sharpened with RED WINE VINEGAR and OREGANO. NO ONIONS ANYWHERE in this dish.

=== THE MEATBALLS (WHAT GOES INSIDE) ===

- ground beef
- MILK-SOAKED (stale) BREAD — the panade
- black pepper
- fresh parsley, chopped
- PARMESAN CHEESE, grated
- GRATED GARLIC
- salt

Mix, shape into meatballs, and brown in olive oil.

=== THE SAUCE ===

- white wine (for the deglaze)
- crushed tomatoes OR crushed fire-roasted tomatoes
- red wine vinegar
- oregano

DEGLAZE the browned meatballs with WHITE WINE before adding the crushed tomatoes. Then the vinegar and oregano; simmer until thickened.

=== SERVE ===

Toss with spaghetti.

=== VARIANT E — PASTA PIPERADE (THE SPANISH LEAN — PASS) ===

The blended vegetable-tomato pasta sauce: sauté everything, blend smooth, toss with pasta.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- shallot (over onion — see the color note)
- garlic
- green bell pepper
- carrot
- tomato
- tomato paste (needed IN ADDITION to the tomato — see notes)
- white wine
- miso paste
- oregano
- red chili flakes
- butter + olive oil mix (the sauté fat)
- salt and black pepper

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. SAUTÉ everything in the butter + olive oil mix.
2. ALL GOES IN THE BLENDER — blend smooth.
3. Toss with SPAGHETTI, PENNE, or GNOCCHI.
4. Top with PARMESAN or GRUYERE. LEMON JUICE to brighten if the cheese is too strong.
notes:
=== MERGED 2026-11-13 — THE FIVE-VARIANT TOMATO SAUCE HOUSE ===

The red pasta sauces merged into one italian tomato sauce house. A/B are the ragu side (protein-forward), C/E the protein-free sauce side, D the meatball shape.

=== BUILD-DEPENDENT RULINGS (READ BEFORE SUBSTITUTING) ===

- TOMATO FORMS: CANNED WHOLE TOMATOES are A/B/C's base. CRUSHED TOMATOES are D's base but CLASHING in A and B. TOMATO PASTE is structural in E but CLASHING in A and B. DICED TOMATOES clashing (C's ruling). FRESH TOMATOES are E's. Crushed + paste live in secondary for this reason.
- PARSLEY: structural in D's meatballs; CLASHING in A. Secondary.
- ONIONS: yellow onions are core to A/B/C; ALL ONIONS ARE CLASHING IN D (its no-onion rule — white/red/powder included); E runs on SHALLOTS.
- GARLIC + OLIVE OIL: everywhere EXCEPT C — Marcella's 3-ingredient sauce is butter-only, no garlic, and basil is clashing there too.
- HERBS: thyme + rosemary + oregano OK in A (the no-herb rule was overturned there); THYME IS CLASHING IN E (makes it taste unoriginal) and rosemary too.
- NUTS/SEEDS: walnuts are secondary in A; ALL seeds/nuts are CLASHING in E (the smooth rule).
- CREAM: clashing in A and E — clashing globally.

=== VARIANT A — BOLOGNESE (MARCELLA HAZAN'S RAGU — PASS) — NOTES ===

THE BOLOGNESE SHAPE — WHAT BOTH VARIANTS HAVE IN COMMON:
1. A tomato base (canned tomatoes + often tomato paste; regular canned only — no fire-roasted; that's the meatballs build (variant D)).
2. A protein slot: a MEAT THING — real ground beef (A) or vegan beef at bare minimum (B; ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is best — impossible/beyond is banned). Lentils and mushrooms are secondary/OK (see below).
3. An acid: wine (white in A per Marcella's canonical; red per Nisha) + balsamic finish in B. See WINE note.
4. Soffrito-style FINELY DICED aromatics: yellow onion always in; celery/garlic; carrots in A only.
5. Long simmer intent (3+ hours for A; shorter for B).
6. Dairy: milk in both.
7. Served over pasta.

=== WINE — WHITE AND RED BOTH APPEAR ===

Both white and red wine appear frequently across canonical bolognese recipes:
- VARIANT A (Marcella): WHITE wine, canonically. Milk goes in first as a protective coat; white wine follows.
- VARIANT B: RED wine per Nisha's tradition; either works.
- CROSS-USE: either wine can work in either variant if that's what you have. Sticking to canonical is safer, but the family absorbs either.

Both wines are primary ingredients in this file for that reason.

=== THE MEAT-THING-MINIMUM RULE — VEGAN BEEF IS THE FLOOR; ABBOTS IS BEST; IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND IS BANNED ===

Core rule: some kind of VEGAN BEEF is the BARE MINIMUM for this recipe. It's like a FRENCH BEEF STEW — you need a meat thing, even if it's fake. The old vegetarian protein path (lentils + walnuts) no longer defines the core recipe. ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is the best fake-meat pick — same verdict as [[french-beef-and-mushroom-stew]].

IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND BEEF — BANISHED AGAIN (CLASHING): it tastes good for 30 MINUTES after you make it, but it tastes HORRIBLE THE DAY AFTER — it becomes a GUMMY, CANDY-LIKE thing: not even sweet, just VERY ARTIFICIAL tasting. REMOVING CARROTS ISN'T ENOUGH. (This reverses the earlier reprieve — the carrots-out + balsamic/milk logic addressed the too-sweet problem, but the day-after aging failure is its own thing and it's disqualifying.)

=== CARROTS ARE OUT OF THE CORE RECIPE — TOO SWEET ===

Carrots are out of variant B: TOO SWEET. The soffrito is celery + onion. Carrots remain in variant A only, where Marcella's canonical soffrito keeps them.

=== LENTILS, MUSHROOMS, AND WALNUTS — SECONDARY/OK ===

Lentils, mushrooms, and walnuts are SECONDARY — OK in this recipe (walked forward from 'out entirely but orthogonal'). The allowance is bolognese-specific: they are NOT OK in [[french-beef-and-mushroom-stew]].

IF YOU WANT A MUSHROOM-FORWARD PASTA: see [[alfredo]] variant B (mushrooms on top). Boscaiola — the rich cream + tomato paste + brandy expression — was retired 2026-11-13 (overly complicated); pasta al funghi, the lean expression, was deleted 2026-11-06. Lentil ragu history lives in the CONTEXT notes below.

=== HERBS — THE NO-HERB RULE IS OVERTURNED FOR THE CORE RECIPE ===

THYME + OREGANO are PRIMARY in variant B now (both were previously marked clashing — reversed). ROSEMARY goes well here WHEN THERE'S ACTUAL MEAT in it.

Variant A stays herb-free per Marcella — the long simmer + milk-and-nutmeg register is its own thing, and fresh herb finishes don't take.

Parsley stays clashing: a porcini powder/mushroom/parsley braise (Marcella — now [[marcella-mushrooms]]) would be good AS A SIDE to this — parsley doesn't need integration into the sauce itself.

=== PORCINI + NOOCH IF VEGETARIAN ===

When made vegetarian (abbots/vegan beef), the recipe benefits from PORCINI MUSHROOM POWDER + NUTRITIONAL YEAST — glutamate support for what the real meat would otherwise bring. Following [[pub-style-lentils]] rules (porcini powder adds glutamates without tipping the scales), A LOT of porcini powder makes a difference here. (Whole mushrooms are secondary now — see the lentils/mushrooms/walnuts note.)

=== VARIANT B NOTES ===

WHERE NISHA IS WRONG, AND WHERE SHE'S RIGHT: her tomato-paste-forward sauce is the miss — this dish wants CANNED TOMATO SAUCE (half a can) with enough milk to read CREAMY, not a paste-dark reduction. But she knocks it out of the park with the BALSAMIC VINEGAR — the dish is incomplete without it. MILK AND BALSAMIC BOTH STAY — confirmed on the latest rework.

MILK, NOT CREAM: heavy cream would be clashing here — MILK is the most appropriate dairy. (Marcella's call stands across both variants: milk's lighter body protects and loosens without tipping the sauce into a cream-sauce register.)

BITTERNESS WATCH — WALNUTS AND NUTMEG: both can embitter. Toasted-but-not-overdone walnuts (secondary now), and a measured hand on the nutmeg.

CHEESE IN THE POT: funky GRUYERE preferred over parmesan, melted in at the end (matches the grating preference for variant A).

=== DISTINCTION FROM FIRE-ROASTED-MEATBALLS ===

Split off from this file. That dish uses fire-roasted tomatoes (load-bearing) and the meatball shape (load-bearing). Neither belongs in bolognese-shape.

=== DISTINCTION FROM LENTIL-MUSHROOM-STEW ===

That dish is a stew, not a ragu — broth-forward, served as a soup, explicitly anti-canned-tomato and anti-tomato-paste, uses stock not pasta. The lentils that used to live in this file's vegetarian variant point there and to [[french-lentils]] now.

=== WHY BOLOGNESE GETS THE HEADLINE ===

Variant A is the canonical italian ragu — Marcella Hazan's recipe is the cookbook's reference point. The three non-negotiables (don't brown the beef, milk before wine, three-hour uncovered simmer) define what 'bolognese' means here. Variant B borrows the bolognese shape as my own core recipe — it respects the shape without trying to be a copy of Marcella.

NO FIRE-ROASTED TOMATOES IN THIS FILE: regular canned tomatoes only. Fire-roasted is the signature of the meatballs build (variant D).

TAGLIATELLE OVER SPAGHETTI FOR VARIANT A: Marcella was explicit that bolognese is for tagliatelle, not spaghetti. The wide flat noodle holds the meat sauce; spaghetti slides under it. Variant B is more forgiving — long-cut still preferred but ridged tubes (rigatoni, penne rigate) work fine.

GRUYERE OVER PARMESAN FOR GRATING ON TOP — MY PREFERENCE: I prefer grated gruyere over grated parmesan as the finishing cheese. The funkiness agrees with the sauce.

=== CONTEXT — NISHA VORA'S LENTIL BOLOGNESE (REFERENCE) ===

Nisha Vora, Rainbow Plant Life — the recipe the old vegetarian variant grew out of. Her build: onions browned with water-deglazing, garlic + oregano + thyme, a whole TUBE of tomato paste caramelized dark, red wine deglaze, 3 cups vegetable broth, 1 cup soaked RED lentils + 1/4 cup toasted crushed walnuts, canned crushed tomatoes, ~35-40 min simmer, 1 tbsp aged balsamic finish, parsley garnish. Her load-bearing claims, kept for reference: TUBE tomato paste over canned (canned reads tinny); soak the red lentils 30-60 min; TOAST the walnuts (raw walnut doesn't deliver — same as the retired lentil wellington's lesson); quality balsamic or skip (cheap balsamic is watery sourness); a commenter found it acidic without dairy — which the milk-and-tomato-sauce rework addresses directly.

=== HISTORICAL NOTE — THE LENTIL/WALNUT AND MUSHROOM VARIANTS REMOVED ===

This file has walked through: four variants (Marcella; my mix; ATK mushroom; mushroom+lentil), then two (Marcella; lentil+walnut vegetarian), now two again with the vegetarian protein path replaced by the meat-thing-minimum rule. Mushrooms read stew; lentils now read as their own dish family. Both were orthogonal to bolognese for a while, then walked forward to secondary/OK (2026-11-04) — the same pass that banished impossible/beyond for its day-after aging failure.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- boscaiola (retired 2026-11-13, overly complicated): was the mushroom-forward pasta home (pasta al funghi, the lean sibling, deleted earlier). The mushroom-pasta slot now lives in [[alfredo]] variant B.
- the meatballs build (variant D): fire-roasted tomatoes + meatball shape. Different shape.
- tomato pasta sauce family — the gnocchi sauce (variant C) and the piperade (variant E) (the survivors): the protein-free italian pasta-sauce side. This bolognese file is the protein-forward, long-simmered counterpart.

=== VARIANT B — WEEKNIGHT VEGETARIAN RAGU (PASS) — NOTES ===

=== THE SUBSTRATE SYSTEM ===

Restructured (September 2026) from a one-pan dish into a WEEK-LONG SUBSTRATE: the pasta + crumbles + garlic + herb base gets made once at maximum volume, lives in a tub, and individual portions get finished as variant A (tomato + vegetable) or variant B (vegan cream). Still the most natural way to use SOY BEEF CRUMBLES, which can be hard to place — the crumbles disappear into the base and let the finishing sauce lead.

=== WHOLE TOMATOES — TOMATO PASTE IS CLASHING ===

You really want WHOLE tomatoes here (canned, regular or fire-roasted — not crushed). Tomato paste is CLASHING.

=== FLEXIBILITY IS THE POINT ===

Any ingredient can basically be omitted. Any noodle works — SPAGHETTI is my pick. Parmesan over the top.

=== SILKEN TOFU — KILLED (2026-11-06) ===

The vegan silken tofu sauce option in variant B is killed — the silken-tofu pasta line just needs work in general (chard pickle pasta was retired in the same pass). Variant B runs on cashew cream.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- the bolognese build (variant A) / the meatballs build (variant D): the real-deal ragus — long-simmered, protein-forward. This is the no-ceremony weeknight end of that family.
- [[ratatouille]]: the same vegetable crowd (eggplant/pepper/tomato), french and vegetable-first instead of crumble-and-noodle.

=== VARIANT C — MARCELLA GNOCCHI SAUCE (THE 3-INGREDIENT SAUCE — PASS) — NOTES ===

Marcella Hazan's 3-ingredient tomato sauce (Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking). Split out from the former italian-tomato-sauces.json (Variant A) into its own file, and RENAMED 'MARCELLA GNOCCHI SAUCE' (September 2026): she recommends this basic tomato/onion/butter sauce for GNOCCHI in particular, and it's very simple — no blender required. That's the niche that kept it on the menu when the rest of the tomato-sauce family retired.

=== THE REST OF THE FAMILY IS RETIRED ===

Sicilian pesto rosso, vodka sauce, and marcella eggplant sauce were moved to retired/ (pasta piperade went too but was later unretired — it kept getting made) (September 2026): they just never make it onto the menu — the amount of effort required for very little nutrition, and awkward leftovers. This sauce survives on the opposite math: minimal effort, no blender, and a specific job (gnocchi).

=== WHY IT WORKS WITH ONLY THREE INGREDIENTS ===

Hazan's insight is that a whole peeled canned tomato + butter + onion, given enough time (~45 min uncovered), builds a sauce that reads more complex than the ingredient list suggests. Butter adds richness and rounds acidity in a way olive oil can't at this simplicity. The onion halves perfume the sauce without becoming a chunky component — that's why they go in whole and come out before serving. No garlic, no basil, no oregano, no chili — the restraint is the recipe.

=== DON'T CHOP THE ONION ===

The onion halves are meant to be discarded. Chopping the onion turns it into part of the sauce texture and changes the dish.

=== UNSALTED BUTTER, GENEROUS ===

Hazan calls for 5 tablespoons per 28-oz can. Don't cut it — the butter is doing structural work, not just flavor. Unsalted so you control the seasoning.

=== SAN MARZANO IF POSSIBLE ===

Whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes are what the recipe was tuned to. Other whole peeled canned tomatoes work; diced canned tomatoes read watery here.

=== FORMER SIBLINGS (ALL IN retired/) ===

- sicilian-pesto-rosso: raw blended sun-dried-tomato + almond pesto.
- vodka-sauce: tomato paste + cream cross-family outlier.
- the piperade (variant E): blended vegetable-tomato base — UNRETIRED September 2026 (it kept getting made).
- marcella-eggplant-sauce: fried eggplant folded into a garlic-tomato base. Also Marcella.

=== DIFFERENTIATION FROM THE RAGU FAMILY ===

This recipe and its siblings tagged 'tomato pasta sauce' are deliberately narrow — protein-free tomato sauces, whole-or-blended (never knife-diced into discrete chunks). For protein-forward, long-simmered, cutting-board-cut counterparts, see the ragu family: the bolognese build (variant A), the meatballs build (variant D).

=== VARIANT D — SPAGHETTI AND MEATBALLS (UNATTEMPTED) — NOTES ===

=== RENAMED (SEPTEMBER 2026) ===

Formerly 'fire roasted meatballs' — renamed now that fire-roasted is the optional smoky direction rather than the identity, and the dish is the classic. (Before that it was an impossible-meat build; git history has both.)

=== THE MEATBALL INTERIOR — THE FULL STACK ===

Inside the meatballs: milk-soaked bread, pepper, parsley, parmesan cheese, and grated garlic (plus the beef and salt). The bread-in-milk panade keeps them tender; the parmesan and garlic season from within; parsley is the herb inside the meatball, oregano the herb on the sauce side.

=== NO ONIONS — ANYWHERE ===

Onions shouldn't appear anywhere in this dish — not in the meatballs, not in the sauce. Clashing.

=== SAUCE — CRUSHED TOMATOES, FIRE-ROASTED OPTIONAL ===

Crushed tomatoes are the base; crushed FIRE-ROASTED tomatoes are the equally valid smoky direction. Red wine vinegar and oregano are both primary — the vinegar sharpens the sauce. Tomato paste stays out.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- the bolognese build (variant A): the other ragu — ground meat loose in the sauce rather than shaped. The meatball-per-forkful format is what this recipe is for.
- the weeknight ragu (variant B): the no-ceremony weeknight end of the family.
- the gnocchi sauce (variant C): the protein-free tomato-sauce side.

=== VARIANT E — PASTA PIPERADE (THE SPANISH LEAN — PASS) — NOTES ===

=== UNRETIRED (SEPTEMBER 2026) ===

Retired with the rest of the tomato-sauce family, then brought back: I just find myself MAKING IT A LOT — which means it should stay.

=== TOMATO PASTE + TOMATO, BOTH — UNLIKE RATATOUILLE ===

Unlike [[ratatouille]], this needs TOMATO PASTE in addition to the tomato. The blend thins the fresh tomato out; the paste holds the backbone.

=== SHALLOT OVER ONION — THE COLOR RULE ===

Shallot over onion so the sauce RETAINS ITS RED/ORANGE COLOR better. (Same color-consciousness as the old mossy-green bouillon lesson — blended sauces show their inputs.)

=== WHITE WINE + MISO — THE FUNK, NECESSARY ===

White wine and miso paste are NECESSARY for funk — and they're better in THIN SAUCES like this one, where they don't taste like stew. (The silent-ingredient discipline applies to the miso as always.)

=== HERBS — OREGANO; THYME UNORIGINAL; ROSEMARY NO ===

OREGANO is the herb. THYME makes it taste UNORIGINAL; ROSEMARY wouldn't work at all (nothing here for it to grip — consistent with the lentil-stew rosemary rule (see [[french-lentils]])).

=== SMOOTH — NO SEEDS OR NUTS ===

Seeds and nuts are clashing across the board — this sauce should be SMOOTH; anything that leaves grit or body in the blend is wrong.

=== CREAM IS CLASHING ===

No cream — it causes you to LOSE THE INTRICATE FLAVOR OF THE CARROT/BELL PEPPER and pushes it into a more generic creamy tomato sauce. The vegetable intricacy is the point of the blend; cream flattens it.

=== LEMON JUICE — THE CHEESE CORRECTION ===

Lemon juice brightens the sauce if the cheese reads too strong. Correction move, not structural.

=== WANT TO TRY ===

- VODKA instead of the white wine (the vodka-sauce logic pointed at this thinner chassis).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[ratatouille]]: the same vegetable family unblended — and no tomato paste there.
- the gnocchi sauce (variant C): the surviving minimal tomato sauce; this is the maximal-blend end.
- the weeknight ragu (variant B): the chunky weeknight cousin.
original_chef: Variant A: Marcella Hazan (Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking). Variant B: Nisha Vora (Rainbow Plant Life). Variant C: Marcella Hazan — the 3-ingredient tomato sauce.
